title.en: Supply of money and its measures

hook.en: You pay a shopkeeper by UPI. No note or coin changes hands, yet the payment is made. So *money* is more than currency. How does the RBI measure the money in the economy?
hook.kn: ನೀವು UPI ಮೂಲಕ ಅಂಗಡಿಯವನಿಗೆ ಹಣ ಪಾವತಿಸುತ್ತೀರಿ. ನೋಟು ನಾಣ್ಯ ಕೈ ಬದಲಾಯಿಸುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಆದರೂ ಪಾವತಿ ಆಗುತ್ತದೆ. ಹಣ ಎಂದರೆ ಚಲಾವಣೆ ನೋಟುಗಳಿಗಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು. RBI ಆರ್ಥಿಕತೆಯ ಹಣವನ್ನು ಹೇಗೆ ಅಳೆಯುತ್ತದೆ?

title.en: Define money supply as a stock
Explain currency as fiat money and legal tender
State M1, M2, M3 and M4

say.en: You pay a shopkeeper by UPI. No note or coin changes hands, yet the payment is made. So money is more than currency. How does the RBI measure the money in the economy? In this lesson: Define money supply as a stock.
Explain currency as fiat money and legal tender.
State M1, M2, M3 and M4.

body.en: *Money supply* is the total stock of money held by the public at a point of time. The public means households, firms and others, excluding the producers of money: the government and the banking system. Currency notes and coins are fiat money: they have value because the government says so. They are legal tender: no one can refuse them in settling a payment.
body.kn: ಹಣದ ಪೂರೈಕೆ ಎಂದರೆ ಒಂದು ಸಮಯದಲ್ಲಿ ಸಾರ್ವಜನಿಕರ ಬಳಿಯಿರುವ ಹಣದ ಒಟ್ಟು ದಾಸ್ತಾನು. ನೋಟು ಮತ್ತು ನಾಣ್ಯಗಳು ಆದೇಶ ಹಣ (ಫಿಯಟ್ ಹಣ); ಅವು ಕಾನೂನುಬದ್ಧ ಚಲಾವಣೆ ಹಣ, ಪಾವತಿಗೆ ಯಾರೂ ನಿರಾಕರಿಸುವಂತಿಲ್ಲ.

Legal tender: cannot be refused for payment.
Cheques are not legal tender.

title.en: On the board: Measuring money supply

say.en: Money supply is the stock held by the public, not by the government or banks. M1 is the narrowest.
M2 adds post office savings deposits. M3 adds net time deposits of banks. M4 adds all post office deposits.
Example: currency 35, demand deposits 25, other deposits 2. M1 is 62.
So M1 is 62, M2 is 67 and M3 is 242 thousand crore.

text.en: M1, M2 narrow; M3, M4 broad

text.en: Currency notes held by the public
Savings deposits with post office savings banks
Net time (fixed) deposits of commercial banks
Total deposits with post office savings organisations (excluding NSCs)

explanation.en: M1 = currency + net demand deposits + other deposits with RBI. M2 adds post office savings deposits to M1; M3 adds banks' net time deposits to M1; M4 adds all post office savings deposits to M3. M3 is the measure most used.

say.en: Measures of money supply Sort each item by the first measure of money supply M1 to M4 that includes it.
say.kn: ಪ್ರತಿ ಅಂಶವನ್ನು ಅದನ್ನು ಮೊದಲು ಸೇರಿಸುವ ಅಳತೆಯ (M1-M4) ಪ್ರಕಾರ ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ.

body.en: The RBI publishes four *measures*. M1 is currency held by the public plus net demand deposits with banks plus other deposits with the RBI. M2 is M1 plus savings deposits with post office savings banks. M3 is M1 plus net time deposits of commercial banks. M4 is M3 plus total deposits with post office savings organisations, excluding National Savings Certificates. M1 and M2 are narrow money; M3 and M4 are broad money. M1 is the most liquid; M3 is the most commonly used measure.
body.kn: RBI ನಾಲ್ಕು ಅಳತೆಗಳನ್ನು ಪ್ರಕಟಿಸುತ್ತದೆ. M1 = CU + DD + OD. M2 = M1 + ಅಂಚೆ ಉಳಿತಾಯ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕ್ ಠೇವಣಿ. M3 = M1 + ವಾಣಿಜ್ಯ ಬ್ಯಾಂಕುಗಳ ನಿವ್ವಳ ಅವಧಿ ಠೇವಣಿ. M4 = M3 + ಅಂಚೆ ಉಳಿತಾಯ ಸಂಸ್ಥೆಗಳ ಒಟ್ಟು ಠೇವಣಿ. M1, M2 ಸಂಕುಚಿತ ಹಣ; M3, M4 ವಿಶಾಲ ಹಣ.

points.en: M2 = M1 + post office savings deposits
M3 = M1 + net time deposits of banks
M4 = M3 + total post office deposits (excl. NSC)

problem.en: For an economy (₹ thousand crore): currency with public 35, net demand deposits 25, other deposits with RBI 2, net time deposits of banks 180, savings deposits with post office savings banks 5. Find M1, M2 and M3.

steps.en: M2 = M1 + post office savings deposits = 62 + 5 = 67.

narration.en: Let us work through this together. For an economy (₹ thousand crore): currency with public 35, net demand deposits 25, other deposits with RBI 2, net time deposits of banks 180, savings deposits with post office savings banks 5. Find M1, M2 and M3.

say.en: Let us work through this together. For an economy (₹ thousand crore): currency with public 35, net demand deposits 25, other deposits with RBI 2, net time deposits of banks 180, savings deposits with post office savings banks 5. Find M1, M2 and M3.
M1 equals 35 plus 25 plus 2 equals 62.
M2 equals M1 plus post office savings deposits equals 62 plus 5 equals 67.
M3 equals M1 plus net time deposits equals 62 plus 180 equals 242.
So the answer is M1 equals 62, M2 equals 67, M3 equals 242 (₹ thousand crore).
